narrative:
The model estimated a 55% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is not a certainty, but it is slightly more likely than passing, and the law school treated that risk as sufficient to deny your application.

The strongest factor in the decision was your undergraduate grade point average of 2.70, below the 3.23 average among accepted students. Although it was the most influential feature, its net effect in your case pushed toward passing rather than failing. The second most important factor was your third-year class-rank decile of 3, well below the accepted-student average of 5.79; this pushed the prediction toward failure. Third, your upper-middle family-income bracket also pushed toward failure. Even though 45.4% of accepted students are in that bracket, the model treated it as an added risk signal here. Together, the second and third factors outweighed the countervailing signal from your GPA and produced the 55% failure estimate.

To improve future chances, focus on strengthening your academic record, especially third-year performance and class standing, and seek advising on bar-exam readiness before reapplying. Ask admissions what evidence would best address the model’s concern, and consider delaying reapplication until you can show clearer academic improvement.
